title: Copying the remaining input suffix
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $s$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$, and let $u,r$ be Boolean words. For every Boolean word $p$, output word $o$, and decomposition $x=p r$, running the pairing machine for $|r|+1$ steps from the canonical pairing configuration in its native-copy state, at input position $|p|$, with captured word $u$ and output $o$, yields the halted canonical pairing configuration at input position $|x|$ with the same saved configuration and capture tape and output $or$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
replaced:
Let the native input decompose as $x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} r$ with the pairing
machine in its native-copy state at input position $|p|$. Then exactly $|r| + 1$
steps emit every bit of $r$ and halt on the right blank, leaving all work tapes
and the capture head unchanged.
